rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Standardized Patient Assessment Data (statutory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory requirement (section 1899B(b)(1)(B) and 1886(j)(7)(F)(ii)) that PAC providers submit standardized patient assessment data with respect to admission and discharge (and more frequently if Secretary deems appropriate) using a standardized patient assessment instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1899B(b)(1)(B) specifies categories that standardized patient assessment data must cover: (1) functional status (mobility and self-care at admission and before discharge); (2) cognitive function and mental status (e.g., depression, dementia); (3) special services, treatments, and interventions (ventilator use, dialysis, chemotherapy, central line, TPN); (4) medical conditions and comorbidities (e.g., diabetes, CHF, pressure ulcers); (5) impairments (incontinence, impaired hearing/vision/swallowing); and (6) other categories deemed necessary and appropriate by the Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDOH category of standardized patient assessment data
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation and definition of the Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) category as socioeconomic, cultural, and environmental circumstances that impact health; authorized under section 1899B(b)(1)(B)(vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS previously defined and adopted SDOH in FY 2020 IRF PPS final rule and expanded definition to align with HHS/CDC/OASH/White House definitions. Currently collected SDOH items in IRF-PAI: ethnicity, race, preferred language, interpreter services, health literacy, transportation, and social isolation. Common standards are used across PAC providers (IRFs, SNFs, LTCHs, HHAs) to promote interoperable longitudinal exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed new SDOH items to collect (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to require IRFs to collect and submit four new SDOH standardized patient assessment data elements beginning FY 2028: one Living Situation item; two Food items; and one Utilities item; and to modify one current SDOH item (Transportation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items were selected from the Accountable Health Communities (AHC) HRSN Screening Tool and adapted from tools such as PRAPARE, USDA HFSS, and C-SNAP. Draft items and response options are available in the IRF-PAI Downloads section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living Situation item (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed question: 'What is your living situation today?' with response options: (1) I have a steady place to live; (2) I have a place to live today, but I am worried about losing it in the future; (3) I do not have a steady place to live; (7) Patient declines to respond; (8) Patient unable to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on AHC HRSN Screening Tool and adapted from PRAPARE. Intended to identify housing instability to inform discharge planning, referrals to community organizations, and care transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Food item #1 (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed question: 'Within the past 12 months, you worried that your food would run out before you got money to buy more.' Response options: (1) Often true; (2) Sometimes true; (3) Never True; (7) Patient declines to respond; (8) Patient unable to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapted from USDA 18-item Household Food Security Survey (HFSS) and AHC HRSN Screening Tool. Intended to assess food security/nutrition risk to inform care planning and referrals (e.g., SNAP, food pharmacies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Food item #2 (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed question: 'Within the past 12 months, the food you bought just didn't last and you didn't have money to get more.' Response options: (1) Often true; (2) Sometimes true; (3) Never True; (7) Patient declines to respond; (8) Patient unable to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapted from USDA HFSS and AHC HRSN Screening Tool. Intended as complementary food security question to identify risk of malnutrition and coordinate nutrition-related interventions prior to discharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilities item (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed question: 'In the past 12 months, has the electric, gas, oil, or water company threatened to shut off services in your home?' Response options: (1) Yes; (2) No; (3) Already shut off; (7) Patient declines to respond; (8) Patient unable to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on AHC HRSN Screening Tool and adapted from C-SNAP survey. Intended to identify energy/utility insecurity to link patients to assistance programs (e.g., LIHEAP) and community supports during discharge planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification to Transportation SDOH item (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to modify one of the current SDOH items collected under the SDOH category (the Transportation item) as described in section VII.C.5 of the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details in the proposed rule section referenced; aim is to update item wording/response options to improve capture of transportation-related needs for discharge planning and care coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for HRSN domains (AHC HRSN tool domain selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Domains for the AHC HRSN Screening Tool were chosen based upon literature review and expert consensus using specific criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The domains (housing instability, food insecurity, transportation difficulties, utility assistance needs, interpersonal safety concerns) were selected using these criteria: (1) availability of high-quality scientific evidence linking a given HRSN to adverse health outcomes and increased healthcare utilization, including hospitalizations and associated costs; (2) ability for a given HRSN to be screened and identified in the inpatient setting prior to discharge, addressed by community-based services, and potentially improve healthcare outcomes, including reduced readmissions; and (3) evidence that a given HRSN is not systematically addressed by healthcare providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of evidence base, technical expert panel (TEP), and testing for item selection
rubrics_metrics.description: AHC HRSN Screening Tool development relied on evidence review, compilation of over 50 screening tools (>200 questions), consultation with a technical expert panel, and testing across diverse care delivery sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS states the tool is evidence-based and was informed by practical experience. A TEP of tool developers, researchers, clinicians, community-based organization leaders, and Federal partners refined the question list. The tool was tested across many care delivery sites in diverse U.S. geographies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment and standardization across programs for interoperability
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for adopting SDOH items that align with items in other CMS programs (e.g., Hospital IQR, IPFQR) to promote common standards and definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using common standards aims to promote interoperable exchange of longitudinal information among PAC providers, facilitate coordinated care, continuity in care planning, and discharge planning processes, and reduce administrative burden where possible by aligning data collection requirements across settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes and benefits of collecting SDOH items
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS articulated three significant benefits of ongoing identification of SDOH via standardized assessment items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits include: (1) promoting screening as evidence-based building blocks to support addressing disparities affecting underserved communities; (2) improving health equity by identifying social needs so IRFs can address them with patients, caregivers, and community partners during discharge planning; (3) supporting IRF QRP initiatives by providing data to stratify performance on current and future quality measures and to develop statistical tools (e.g., Health Equity Confidential Feedback Reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing administrative burden against benefits and implementation supports
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS considered commenter concerns about additional administrative burden and weighed increased burden against expected benefits of adopting new SDOH assessment items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS concluded collection is within normal IRF operations (e.g., discharge planning obligations under §482.43(a) and comprehensive plan of care requirements under §412.606), and committed to provide training resources (online modules, tip sheets, Q&A, recorded webinars/videos) in advance of initial collection (anticipating mid-2025 availability) to reduce burden. CMS also explained rationale for not providing additional funding and clarified intent that items document information many IRFs already collect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of SDOH data in discharge planning and comprehensive plan of care
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection of SDOH items is intended to inform the comprehensive plan of care and initiation of discharge planning beginning at admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRFs must identify patients likely to suffer adverse consequences upon discharge and provide discharge planning evaluation; SDOH items can inform interventions (e.g., education on transportation resources, referrals for utilities assistance, nutrition planning) that are part of the comprehensive plan of care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of SDOH data for health equity monitoring and measure stratification
rubrics_metrics.description: SDOH standardized data elements may be used to stratify quality measures and to monitor differences in outcomes by factors such as race/ethnicity and dual-enrollment status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS referenced existing work (Health Equity Confidential Feedback Reports) and noted that additional SDOH data will enable continued development of statistical tools to maximize value of Medicare data and improve care quality for beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to measure removal evaluation process (§412.634(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors used to evaluate whether a measure should be removed from the IRF QRP are referenced in §412.634(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule refers readers to §412.634(b)(2) for a discussion of factors used to evaluate potential removal of a measure from the IRF QRP; details are contained in that regulatory provision (not fully reproduced in this chunk).
